headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: aci can handle CRM/email data and broad egress while Superset has allowlisted egress, creating a plausible shared-data exposure path; prompt injection and capability conflict are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server and touches email/CRM data; Superset can consume data through its API. A shared workspace or MCP bridge is not explicitly documented, so the interaction is inferred and uncertain, but if aci outputs untrusted content into Superset workflows, instruction hijacking is plausible.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into a Superset dashboard, SQL, or note field without sanitization
IF both agents are connected through a shared MCP server or shared workspace
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of aci-generated text into Superset
Require manual review before pasting agent output into dashboards or queries
Add provenance labels to all aci outputs
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add content filtering at the MCP boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; Superset has allowlisted egress and can access analytics APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem or direct data flow, so this is inferred rather than observed, but if shared data reaches Superset, leakage of sensitive business data is plausible.
conditions: IF aci and Superset share a workspace, database, or exported files containing CRM/email data
IF Superset is configured to ingest or display those files or records
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive tables
Remove CRM/email exports from shared locations
Audit outbound destinations for aci
requires-engineering: enforce row-level and dataset-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while Superset has allowlisted egress and only exposes the Superset API. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not established; uncertainty remains because shared orchestration is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external system through their APIs
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable dataset without locking
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Avoid shared write targets
Use locking or queueing around shared resources
Review API scopes before deployment
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Superset can consume API-fed analytics outputs. If Superset treats aci output as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream decisions. The profiles do not document verification steps, so the pathway is inferred and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF Superset uses aci-produced records or summaries without validation
IF downstream users act on Superset outputs as if they were verified facts
mitigations: Require human review of aci-derived inputs
Mark aci outputs as untrusted in Superset
Add validation checks before ingestion
Limit aci-derived data to draft views
requires-engineering: implement source-of-truth reconciliation

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and support data and requests OAuth/secrets handling, while Superset's profile shows no touched data classes or special compliance claims. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from aci into Superset without a documented policy basis
IF retention or deletion settings differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents
Avoid sending regulated records to Superset
Document retention settings for both systems
Review OAuth and secret-handling procedures
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
